misconceptions.trigger: learner focuses only on making the course flashy or amusing
misconceptions.feedback: Motivation is broader than fun. ARCS includes attention, relevance, confidence, and satisfaction, all of which shape sustained engagement.

misconceptions.description: Assuming more external rewards always increase motivation
misconceptions.trigger: learner recommends rewards without considering intrinsic interest or autonomy
misconceptions.feedback: External rewards can help in some contexts, but overuse can crowd out intrinsic motivation if learners begin to work only for the incentive.

misconceptions.description: Assuming confidence is built by making tasks trivial
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates confidence design with removing challenge altogether
misconceptions.feedback: Confidence comes from achievable challenge, clear expectations, and meaningful progress, not from eliminating effort completely.
